newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Eindhoven airport to talk to agents on cargo plan.
newsitem.headline: Eindhoven airport to talk to agents on cargo plan.

text.p: Eindhoven airport said it will next month embark on talks with local regional freight forwarders in a bid to implement recommendations of a report into the future of flown air cargo at the airport.
The report, entitled 'Reaching for the Skies in Air Cargo', studies the potential of flown air cargo specifically at Eindhoven airport.
Conducted by Erasmus University in Rotterdam and presented recently to the airport, the study aims to develop an outline marketing plan for the development of flown air cargo.

The report finds that on the basis of a questionnaire amongst major air cargo shippers in the area, there was definitely solid demand for air cargo services, with a total potential market of around 75,000 tonnes a year identified.
This potential mainly arose from the manufacturing and horticultural sectors. Of the cargo volumes, 80 percent would comprise outbound tonnage and 20 percent, inbound.
The report envisages a scenario whereby Eindhoven airport's cargo by air would amount to around 7,800 tonnes a year, based on a weekly intercontinental freighter service.
The remainder of the projected 75,000 tonnes focuses on trucked cargo.
In the Eindhoven region there is a large concentration of companies producing hi-tech equipment, machines, components and parts.
Eindhoven is the home of electronics giant Phillips.
The report says that several regional shippers expressed interest in new cargo initiatives at Eindhoven Airport, it stated.
It concludes that if Eindhoven was to accommodate a larger volume of cargo by air, it should develop into a sub-hub within the network of a large forwarder operating contract freighter services.
However, the report warns that Eindhoven Airport Authority would need to redefine its focus on cargo operations.

Initially, the airport authority should develop constructive business-to-business dialogue with shippers, forwarders and airlines, as well as with the local cargo handling company and customs, the report finds.
"It is essential that the airport formulates a clear cargo strategy and that it constructs an airport product that supports the sub-hub type of operations envisaged," it states.
